name: Awaab's Law hazard triage and statutory clock
organisation_name: Synthetic example body — not a real landlord
significant_effect_note: A repair decision, a tenant-facing summary, and a reasonable-endeavours defence can have a significant effect. Those decisions are outside the agent. This row screens the draft triage only.
one_sentence_description: A starter that turns one tenant hazard report into a draft triage, with Awaab's Law dates calculated in Python.
public_description: The tool proposes a hazard family and category, calculates timeframes in code, flags vulnerability characteristics without labelling the tenant, drafts a written summary, and drafts a reasonable-endeavours record from steps an officer entered. The officer approves the category, the clock, and every summary.
detailed_description: src/statutory_clock.py calculates dates. A date is operative only when the officer has confirmed that the home is a social home in England, has approved the category, and has approved the clock, and the phase is in force. Phase 2 and Phase 3 are not given an operative clock. The agent does not send, does not write a housing system, and does not decide that a defence is made out.
benefits: Dates come from code rather than from a model. No reduction in repairs time is claimed.
previous_process: An officer read the report and calculated dates. This repository does not replace a named landlord's process.
alternatives_considered: The clock is the piece that runs in the standard library. A Microsoft Foundry extractor is described and not built.
operational_process: The officer approves the hazard category and the clock before a date is treated as operative, reviews any vulnerability characteristic before it is recorded, and sends or files outside the agent.
human_review: An officer approves the category, the clock, and every tenant-facing summary. The agent does not refer a complaint to the Housing Ombudsman and does not book accommodation.
frequency_and_scale: Not deployed. The synthetic reports are fixtures. That is not an operational volume.
required_training: Not recorded. Officers would need the landlord's own procedure, which is not in this repository.
appeals_and_review: N/A for the agent's output. Referral to the Housing Ombudsman is disabled. The draft can include published escalation information.
system_architecture: Python for the clock and a mock triage. Copilot Studio, Power Platform, and Microsoft Foundry are described. Nothing in the folder calls a model or a housing system.
system_input: One hazard report, an awareness time, and category inputs the officer has approved.
system_output: A draft triage, clock JSON, and a reasonable-endeavours record built only from steps the officer entered.
maintenance: The regulations and guidance were read on 24 October 2026. Phase 2 was still a draft instrument. The manifest next review is 24 April 2027, sooner if commencement changes.
models_summary: No model is called. The mock triage is a keyword stand-in.
model_name: No deployed model. Keyword stand-in for the smoke test.
model_task: Propose a hazard family and category. Dates are not a model task.
model_output: Draft fields and a draft summary. Dates are copied from the clock.
model_architecture: Rule-based keyword stand-in plus a deterministic date calculator. Not a trained model.
model_performance: eval/smoke_report.json is a mock smoke test of the keyword stand-in. It is not a model score.
datasets_and_purposes: Synthetic hazard reports for the smoke test. Not used to train a model.
development_data_description: Invented reports. No landlord is named.
data_quantities: Synthetic cases in the smoke test. Not an operational caseload.
development_sensitive_attributes: Invented text can mention health. No real tenant.
data_completeness: The fixtures are written to exercise the rules. They are not a repairs population.
operational_data_sources: Text and times the officer supplies for one run.
operational_sensitive_attributes: A real report can include health information. The Experiment 05 manifest does not assert an Article 9 condition. The landlord confirms the basis.
operational_data_processing: The clock uses the awareness time and the approved category. It does not clean a data set.
operational_data_access: The starter does not persist the report.
operational_data_sharing: N/A. The agent does not send.
impact_assessments: No DPIA is linked. The manifest names Article 6(1)(c) as a lead basis for the landlord to confirm. It does not assert Article 6(1)(e) for every landlord, and it does not assert an Article 9 condition.
risks_and_mitigations: A wrong category or an invented date can miss a statutory timeframe. The officer approves the category and the clock. Phases that are not in force are not given an operative date.
